definitions.explanation: In grammar, the noun or phrase that receives the action of a verb. In Japanese, the direct object is typically marked with the particle を.

examples.japanese: 「⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{目的語|もくてきご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{文|ぶん}→文：03716_bun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{目的語|もくてきご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦どれ→どれ：00547_dore⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Which is the object in this sentence?

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{目的語|もくてきご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{動詞|どうし}→動詞：03472_doushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{普通|ふつう}→普通：01502_futsuu⟧だ。
examples.english: In Japanese, the object normally comes before the verb.

notes:
A grammar term composed of ⟦{目的|もくてき}→目的：02433_mokuteki⟧ (purpose, objective) + ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (word). Used in both Japanese grammar instruction and when discussing foreign language grammar.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{直接|ちょくせつ}→直接：03499_chokusetsu⟧{目的語|もくてきご}: direct object
- ⟦{間接|かんせつ}→間接：00180_kansetsu⟧{目的語|もくてきご}: indirect object
- {目的語|もくてきご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to take an object (said of a verb)
- {目的語|もくてきご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{省略|しょうりゃく}→省略：03244_shouryaku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to omit the object

USAGE:
In Japanese grammar, the concept of {目的語|もくてきご} maps roughly to the noun phrase marked by ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧. However, Japanese linguistic tradition sometimes analyzes sentence structure differently from Western grammar, so the term is most commonly encountered in foreign language education or comparative grammar.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{主語|しゅご}→主語：00377_shugo⟧: subject — the doer of the action
- ⟦{述語|じゅつご}→述語：04274_jutsugo⟧: predicate — the part of the sentence that describes the action or state
- ⟦{補語|ほご}→補語：22867_hogo⟧: complement — a grammatical element that completes the meaning of the predicate
